intro: Lesson 63: Sound waves and the Doppler effect. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: A car approaches you sounding its horn at 400 Hz. You hear...
questions.a: C) Above 400 Hz. Waves are compressed in front of the moving source, so the observed frequency is higher.

questions.q: v = fλ: 340 m/s, 170 Hz gives λ =?
Sound waves are made of compressions and...
Explain why sound cannot travel in a vacuum.
questions.a: Sound is a vibration of particles (1); a vacuum has no particles to pass on the vibrations (1)
questions.model: What carries sound? Vibrating particles of a medium. What is in a vacuum? Nothing. So no vibrations can pass on.

questions.q: Echo returns after 0.4 s at 340 m/s. Distance to the wall?
What happens to the observed wavelength as a source moves away?

A train sounds a horn of frequency 500 Hz. (a) Describe and explain what a person on the platform hears as the train approaches and then passes [4]. (b) Calculate the wavelength of the 500 Hz sound in still air at 340 m/s [2].
questions.a: (a) higher pitch as it approaches (1) because wavefronts are compressed/shorter wavelength (1); lower pitch after passing (1) because wavelength is stretched (1); (b) λ = 340 ÷ 500 = 0.68 m (2)
questions.model: Teacher answers the first mark: 'As the train approaches, the person hears a higher frequency than 500 Hz.'

questions.q: Why does sound travel faster in water than in air?
questions.a: Particles are closer together (1), so vibrations are passed on more quickly (1)

questions.q: How do police speed guns use the Doppler effect?
questions.a: They measure the frequency change of reflected radio or microwave signals from a moving car to calculate its speed.
